The only paths to success require being exactly one of athletic or scholarly. Gwen reads widely → scholarly (from if reads widely → scholarly). So Gwen is scholarly.

Because Gwen is scholarly, the disjunction "athletic xor scholarly" is true (only scholarly). Hence, by the conditional, Gwen is successful. 

Now use: If successful and works hard → achieves goals. Gwen is successful and works hard → Gwen achieves goals.

Finally: If eats well or achieves goals → stays healthy. Gwen achieves goals, so Gwen stays healthy.

But the earlier rule said: Gwen gets enough rest or stays healthy, and not both. Gwen stays healthy, so Gwen does NOT get enough rest.

Now check rest derivation: If exercises regularly and manages stress → gets enough rest. Gwen exercises regularly and manages stress, so we must conclude Gwen gets enough rest. But we just derived Gwen does NOT get enough rest. Contradiction.

Hence, the context (given additions) is inconsistent. In classical logic an inconsistent set of premises entails every proposition, including 'Gwen is athletic.' Thus, the conclusion is entailed.
